issues.description: The left thumb is not straight in 3D, and the report does not say so. The thumb metacarpal (CMC to MCP) runs along the hand's long axis at 26.4 deg in the image; the wrist-to-palm axis is at 25 deg. The thumb then turns 24.8 deg sideways at the MCP, in the plane of its nail, with 0.9 deg of hyperextension. The IP turns 7.9 deg sideways the other way on top of its 27.2 deg flexion, so the chain zigzags +25 / -8. The drawn thumb is straight: the keypoints give 41.2 / 46.3 / 45.0 deg, and the thumb comes diagonally out of the base of the palm, as D2 describes it. A 25 deg sideways MCP bend with the joint fully extended is at or beyond the joint's normal range. The fit produced this by pushing thumb_cmc 42.8 px (2.86u of the 3u gate) toward the wrist. That lays the thenar mass, which the builder aligns with the metacarpal, along the palm-heel outline, which is fitted to 2 px. Earlier poses had 10.4 deg (fe37dea) and 18.1 deg (R7). The kink is hidden inside the thenar mass in all 8 views rendered. Its visible trace is the thenar lying along the hand axis, with the groove above it. The calibrator put hinge constraints on the fingers only; the pose notes and the report cover only the thumb's bone lengths and nail angle. This trades thumb anatomy against silhouette pixels beyond the stated constraints, and nobody was asked, so per the task it is rated major and put to the user. No single pose edit clearly fixes it. Straightening empties the palm-heel outline: p95 6.3 / 5.0, and 2.236 at best with thenar_size 1.25 and palm_heel_px 52. It also pushes sideways bend into the IP hinge (-9.9 to -11.9 deg), because the builder takes the thumb frame from the metacarpal direction.

decisionsForUser.question: Left thumb (D2's defining digit): in the calibrated pose the thumb metacarpal lies along the hand's axis and the thumb turns about 25 deg sideways at the MCP. The drawing shows a straight thumb coming diagonally out of the base of the palm. The kink is hidden inside the thenar mass. Its visible trace is the thenar lying along the hand axis, with a groove about 10 ref px deep above it. Straightening the thumb costs the palm-heel outline (contour p95), because the builder places the thenar along the thumb metacarpal and takes the thumb's frame from it. Accept the thumb as it is, refit it with a straightness constraint, or ask the builder first?
options: A: accept as calibrated. Every gate passes. The thumb MCP stays 24.8 deg sideways and hidden in the thenar, thumb_cmc stays at 2.86u, and the groove stays as a minor.

B: refit the thumb with a constraint (for example MCP sideways <= about 12 deg, IP sideways <= about 5 deg, thumb_cmc toward its reading (430,330)), and refit the thenar, palm heel and wrist crease to the palm-heel outline. The verifier's rough attempts reached p95 2.236 (gate 2.0) at MCP 16.5 deg, but with IP sideways -9.9 deg. It may plateau, in which case D6 applies.

C: builder first (a step-3-style request). Let the thenar and palm heel be oriented and placed independently of the thumb metacarpal, and take the thumb frame from the nail rather than from the metacarpal direction, so that straightening does not move the bend into the IP. Then refit.

decisionsForUser.recommendation: B, bounded to one refit attempt: straighten the thumb (thumb_cmc toward its reading), include the thumb-end shortening that e7 shows passes every gate, and refit the palm heel and thenar. If p95 plateaus above 2.0, keep the current thumb (A) with the residual recorded (D6), and record C as a builder request for a later round. The user chose hinged anatomy over a pixel-equal fit in D23. The thumb is the digit D2 is defined by, and straightening it would likely also remove the groove.
